title: Point only at steps that exist
statement: Every hint, recap or feedback line that points to another step must name a step that exists, by its current name, and say what that step actually did.
example: In one audit, three wrong-option feedback lines used a step name the lesson had retired.
detail: A curriculum-adherence report on four Grade 3 lessons found a build frame whose hint told students to use one of the words they had locked in at Step 3, a step that did not exist in the served lesson, and a recap meant to mirror the model's thinking whose text described a different task. An external audit of the same lessons found three wrong-option feedback lines using a step name the lesson had retired.
